prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals

- Economy, tax, and regulation:
  - Save £12bn a year by 2007–08 via a civil service recruitment freeze, cutting 235,000 administrative posts, and abolishing or merging 168 public bodies.
  - Grow total public spending by 4% a year to 2011–12; increase or maintain funding for the NHS, schools, transport, international development, police, defence, and pensions.
  - Use £8bn of savings to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts.
  - Halve council tax bills for households where all residents are over 65 (up to £500), funded centrally.
  - Link the basic state pension to earnings; retain existing pensioner benefits. Create Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; encourage “opt‑out” workplace pensions; use unclaimed financial assets to protect failed schemes.
  - Keep an independent central bank; retain the national currency and not join the euro.
  - Reduce regulatory burdens: departmental regulatory budgets, sunset reviews, end “gold‑plating” of EU directives; seek restoration of opt‑outs from certain EU employment rules.

- Childcare and education:
  - Flexible maternity pay (choice of nine months standard or higher rate over six months).
  - Up to £50 per week per child under five for eligible working families regardless of childcare type; support workplace nurseries and after‑school clubs.
  - Invest an extra £15bn per year in schools by 2009–10. Give heads control over admissions and expulsions; create Turnaround Schools; cut paperwork.
  - Simplify funding so money follows the pupil; allow international qualifications; publish marks with grades; slim the National Curriculum.
  - 300,000 vocational grants of £1,000 for 14–16 year‑olds; promote school sport (two hours after school), healthier meals, and safer school trips.
  - Add 600,000 school places in the first term to expand parental choice; allow state funds to follow pupils to low‑cost independent schools.
  - Moratorium on closing special schools; reform further education funding; enable “Super college” status.
  - Abolish university tuition fees and the admissions regulator; promote university endowments.

- Health and social care:
  - Increase NHS funding by £34bn in the first Parliament (to ~£2,000 per head). Cut tiers of management (fewer PCTs, abolish SHAs, reduce quangos); scrap central targets.
  - Greater hospital autonomy; reinstate matrons with authority over cleanliness; expand infection control and single rooms.
  - Patient and GP choice of provider; payment by activity; protect community hospitals. Contribute half the NHS-equivalent cost for self‑pay operations to cut waits; aim to end waiting lists within the Parliament.
  - Social care partnership to avoid forced home sales; more support for carers.
  - Reform NHS dentistry access; offer low monthly payment cover.
  - Health checks for long‑stay immigrants; national STI awareness campaign.

- Crime, justice, and security:
  - Recruit 5,000 additional police officers annually; cut paperwork; introduce elected police commissioners and neighbourhood policing.
  - Add 20,000 prison places; end early release; transparent minimum custodial terms.
  - Expand drug treatment, including 25,000 residential rehab places; reclassify cannabis to Class B.
  - Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; strengthen counter‑terror powers; tighten extradition/deportation processes.

- Immigration and borders:
  - 24/7 port surveillance; restore embarkation controls; create a unified Border Control Police.
  - Australian‑style points system for work permits.
  - Process asylum applications outside the UK; set an annual overall migration limit and a parliamentary asylum quota; take refugees via UNHCR. Seek changes to EU/international arrangements, including the 1951 Convention.

- Governance and devolution:
  - Publish a delivery timetable and enforce ministerial accountability.
  - Abolish regional assemblies; return planning, housing, transport, and fire powers to local authorities.
  - Strengthen parliamentary scrutiny; reduce MPs by 20%; pursue a substantially elected upper chamber.
  - “English votes for English laws”; uphold devolution settlements; a Welsh referendum on powers; more accountable direct rule if needed in Northern Ireland.

- Communities, transport, environment, and rural:
  - More local control over planning; stronger action on illegal encampments; review the Human Rights Act.
  - Devolve arts and lottery decisions.
  - Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership and equity stakes for social tenants.
  - Modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
  - Protect green belts; prioritise brownfield development.
  - Phase out HFCs; incentives for energy‑efficient homes and low‑emission cars (lower VED, grants); increase recycling; diversify energy with renewables and efficiency.
  - Honest food labelling; require the Little Red Tractor mark for public procurement; pursue CAP and fisheries reform; strengthen animal welfare. Free vote on repealing the hunting ban.

- Defence, foreign policy, and aid:
  - Increase frontline defence spending by £2.7bn by 2007–08; support service families; retain regiments; improve procurement; keep NATO central.
  - Set a referendum on the proposed EU constitution; not join the euro; seek EU reform and specific opt‑outs.
  - Continue commitments in Iraq; support a Middle East two‑state solution.
  - Reach 0.7% of national income for aid by 2013; increase national control over aid; promote open markets and rule of law.

- Early actions promised:
  - Begin recruiting extra police; reinstate matrons; first Budget to cut waste and lower taxes; empower heads on expulsions; start 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU constitution referendum date.
